To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have generated and characterised novel mouse models harbouring loss of parkin and Pacr or Pacrg alone; (2) there were no significant behavioural or dopaminergic deficits in either mutant line compared to wildtype at 18–20 months of age.

we have generated and characterized two novel knockout mouse models harbouring loss of parkin and Pacr g or Pacr g alone, and that there are no significant differences in behaviour and dopaminergic neuronal survival in the substantia nigr a of either mutant line at 18-20 months of age.
the parkin-PacRG knockout mouse line and Pacrg knockout mouse lines do not show any significant differences in behaviour or dopaminergic neuron numbers compared to wild-type littermates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the function of PACGR in a parkin-PACGR double knockout model.
a better understanding of the function of the parkin-Pacreg bidirectionally regulated gene locus.
the role of PACRG and parkin in the pathogenesis of PD, and we have generated novel knockout mice that lack both parkin and PACR or PACRG alone.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the loss of both parkins and PACRG does not result in a phenotype that recapitulates parkin-mediated PD in mice.
there is no evidence to date that parkin and Pacrig function in a common biological pathway.
loss of parkin and PACRg is not sufficient to cause PD-like pathology in mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the absence of PACRG in mice did not result in the loss of dopaminergic function and that PACRG may not be a key component of parkin-mediated PD.
loss of parkin and Pacr g does not result in dopaminergic neuronal dysfunction or loss in mice.
the absence of PACRG does not appear to affect the function of parkin and that the absence of parkin and PACREG does not appear to have a detrimental effect on the dopaminergic nigrostriatal pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
loss of parkin and Pacr g does not appear to be sufficient to recapitulate parkin-associated PD.
PACRG and parkin are not essential for the survival of nigrostriatal dopamine neurons.
the loss of parkin and/or Pacrg does not result in the development of a parkinsonian phenotype in mice.
